items.title: 2 Defensive Healthcare Stocks Hitting New 52-Week Highs: ABBV & LLY
items.summary: AbbVie and Eli Lilly have reached fresh 52-week highs following strong Q3 results, offering defensive healthcare alternatives as technology stocks face valuation concerns. AbbVie benefits from robust immunology drug sales and a 5.2% dividend increase, while Eli Lilly's obesity drug franchise (Mounjaro and Zepbound) drives exceptional 39% revenue growth and raised full-year guidance.

items.title: 4 Healthcare ETFs to Tap Into Eli Lilly's Post-Q3 Earnings Rally
items.summary: Eli Lilly (LLY) jumped 10.1% following better-than-expected Q3 2026 results and raised 2026 sales guidance. The company's blockbuster drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound generated over $16 billion in combined revenues with $6 billion year-over-year growth. However, LLY trades at a premium P/E ratio of 30.91, prompting investors to consider healthcare ETFs with significant LLY weightings as a balanced alternative for exposure.

items.title: LLY Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and Obesity Drug Growth
items.summary: Eli Lilly reported strong Q3 2026 earnings, beating estimates with $7.48 EPS vs. $5.38 consensus and $24.40B revenue (+39% YoY). The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $91-92B from $85-87B, driven by robust demand for obesity and diabetes treatments Mounjaro and Zepbound, which combined for over $16B in sales. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Program has attracted 500,000+ prescriptions since July, with new oral treatment Foundayo generating $184M in Q3 sales. Despite pricing pressures and upcoming manufacturing investments, management remains confident in long-term growth opportunities across its cardiometabolic and broader pipeline.

items.title: LLY's Mounjaro Gets FDA Nod to Cut Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes
items.summary: The FDA has approved Eli Lilly's Mounjaro (tirzepatide) to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes. In a 13,299-patient study, Mounjaro showed an 8% lower MACE-3 rate than Trulicity, meeting non-inferiority objectives. With $18.6B in first-half 2026 sales, this expanded indication could drive further growth and narrow the competitive gap with Novo Nordisk's Ozempic.

items.title: Zealthy Launches Enhanced Weight-Loss Care Platform With Integrated Zepbound Access and Insurance Support
items.summary: Zealthy announced the launch of its enhanced virtual weight-loss care platform that integrates telehealth services, insurance coordination, and prescription management for obesity treatment. The platform enables patients to complete online health assessments and connect with licensed providers who may prescribe Zepbound (tirzepatide), an FDA-approved GLP-1 medication. Zealthy's membership starts at $39 for the first month and $135 thereafter, with medication costs billed separately. With insurance, eligible patients may pay approximately $25 per month for Zepbound.
